what: The Bank of Nova Scotia, known as Scotiabank, is one of Canada's big six banks. Alongside Canadian retail and commercial banking it has the largest Latin American presence of any Canadian bank, in Mexico, Peru, Chile and Colombia.
customers: Canadian households and businesses, and retail and corporate customers across Latin America.
money: deposits, mortgages and commercial lending in Canada
retail and commercial banking in Mexico and the Pacific Alliance countries
moat: Protected positions in both the Canadian oligopoly and in Latin American markets where it has operated for over a century.
risks: Latin American exposure brings currency and political volatility
Canadian mortgage renewals at higher rates raise loan losses
Returns have lagged the other large Canadian banks for years
It has been reshaping the Latin American footprint, selling some markets
opportunities: Redirecting capital from weaker Latin American markets to Canada and Mexico
A dividend yield above 3.5% with a long payment record
watch: International banking credit losses and the return on equity against Canadian peers.
